newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian parliament approves Jewish compensation.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian parliament approves Jewish compensation.

text.p: Hungary's parliament has approved a law which Jewish leaders said on Wednesday set the stage for final talks with the government on compensation for property lost in the Holocaust.

The parliament passed a law on Tuesday creating a public foundation to administer property confiscated from Hungarian Jews during World War Two and to oversee payments to elderly Jewish survivors of the Nazi campaign to exterminate the Jews.
Peter Feldmajer, president of the Confederation of Hungarian Jewish Communities, said he hoped this month will see the end of negotiations.

Feldmajer said the way was now cleared for the Jewish community to negotiate with the government on the amount of monetary compensation and property, including buildings and other valuables, to be turned over to the Jewish community.

Feldmajer told Reuters the government had proposed giving four billion forints ($25 million) in compensation coupons to supplement pensions of the estimated 20,000 Hungarian Jewish survivors of the Holocaust.

"It's not enough, it's nothing. It's a first little step," Feldmajer said. "We must negotiate who will be on the governing board of the foundation and -- the most important thing -- what is the money it will have."
He also said the government had yet to specify which buildings it proposed to return to the Jewish community.
"The government should say something, what kind of buildings and we will think about whether it is a good building or a bad building," Feldmajer said.
Hungary, before World War Two, had an estimated 800,000 to one million Jews, one of the wealthiest Jewish communities in Europe.
The Hungarian government agreed to establish the public foundation in July after talks with the World Jewish Congress and other groups, but the act needed parliamentary approval.
